Package com.nexuslink.ui.files

Class TransferQueue

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.ui.files.TransferQueue
public final class TransferQueue extends Object
Drives the existing FileTransfer copy logic for a batch of TransferItems, exposing observable per-item and overall progress. The mechanics of moving bytes are NOT re-implemented here — each item is dispatched to FileTransfer.upload(java.nio.file.Path, java.lang.String, java.util.function.LongConsumer)/FileTransfer.download(com.nexuslink.ui.files.FileItem, java.nio.file.Path, java.util.function.LongConsumer). Transfers run one at a time by default; setConcurrency(int) lets several run in parallel across a pool of worker threads (each item is claimed atomically so no two workers take the same file).

This class is JavaFX-free and therefore unit-testable: tests drive it synchronously via runPending() with a LocalFileSystem on both sides, while the UI calls startWorker() once so transfers run on a background thread.

    • enqueue

      public List<TransferItem> enqueue(TransferItem.Direction direction, List<FileItem> sources, String destDir, OverwriteResolver resolver, boolean moveMode)
      Enqueues a batch. When moveMode is true each file is a move: its source is deleted once the copy completes successfully (a copy that is skipped or fails leaves the source untouched).

    • enqueueRecursive

      public List<TransferItem> enqueueRecursive(TransferItem.Direction direction, List<FileItem> sources, String destRootDir, OverwriteResolver resolver) throws Exception
      Expands any directories in sources recursively and enqueues every file they contain, recreating the folder structure under destRootDir on the destination side; plain files are enqueued straight into destRootDir. The source tree is read via the appropriate FileSystem (local for an upload, remote for a download) and the matching destination directories are created with FileSystem.mkdir(java.lang.String) as needed.

      Performs blocking I/O (listing the source tree + creating destination directories), so callers must invoke it off the UI thread. Directories are created up-front; the enqueued files then flow through the normal sequential worker with the shared resolver.

      Throws:
      Exception

    • cancel

      public boolean cancel(TransferItem item)
      Cancels a still-pending item. A QUEUED item is marked CANCELLED so the worker skips it; an item already ACTIVE or terminal is left alone (the in-flight copy can't be interrupted mid-stream). Returns true if the item was cancelled.

    • retry

      Re-queues a single FAILED/CANCELLED item; no-op for DONE/SKIPPED/QUEUED/ACTIVE.

    • move

      public boolean move(TransferItem item, int delta)
      Moves a still-QUEUED item one slot earlier (delta < 0) or later (delta > 0) in the queue, so the user can reprioritise pending transfers. Only reorders relative to other QUEUED items; ACTIVE/terminal items keep their place and are never displaced. Returns true if the item actually moved.

    • startWorker

      public void startWorker()
      Starts concurrency() daemon workers that drain the queue as items arrive, so up to that many files transfer in parallel. Idempotent — the worker count is fixed at start; call stopWorker() then startWorker() again to apply a new concurrency.

    • setVerifyIntegrity

      public void setVerifyIntegrity(boolean verify)
      When enabled, each completed file is verified with TransferIntegrity by comparing the destination's byte count against the source size; a mismatch (or a missing destination) marks the item FAILED so it can be retried. Off by default since it lists the destination directory per file.

    • isVerifyIntegrity

      public boolean isVerifyIntegrity()

    • setVerifyChecksum

      public void setVerifyChecksum(boolean verify)
      Strengthens the integrity check from "same size" to "same bytes" by hashing both copies (Checksum.ALGORITHM) and comparing the digests, catching corruption that preserves length. Only has an effect while isVerifyIntegrity() is on, and only for files both sides can hash (FileSystem.canChecksum(com.nexuslink.ui.files.FileItem)) — when either cannot, that file quietly falls back to the size check rather than failing on a check that was never available.

      Off by default, and materially more expensive than the size check: it re-reads both copies in full, so a verified upload moves roughly three times the file's bytes.

    • isVerifyChecksum

      public boolean isVerifyChecksum()

    • setResumeTransfers

      public void setResumeTransfers(boolean resume)
      When enabled, a retried transfer appends to whatever partial file its interrupted attempt left at the destination instead of re-sending from byte zero — the difference between losing ten minutes of a large upload and losing ten seconds. Only applies on a retry (a first attempt's pre-existing destination file belongs to the overwrite resolver) and only where the transport can append (FileTransfer.supportsResume()); everything else transfers whole files as before.

      Off by default because resuming trusts the partial bytes to be a correct prefix of the source — see ResumePlan for why a source edited between attempts can produce a right-sized but spliced file, and why setVerifyChecksum(boolean) is the companion that catches it.

    • isResumeTransfers

      public boolean isResumeTransfers()

    • setAutoRetry

      public void setAutoRetry(RetryPolicy policy)
      Enables automatic retry of transfers that fail with a transient error (TransferErrors.isTransient(java.lang.Throwable)) according to policy, backing off between attempts. A permanent error (bad credentials, missing file) still fails immediately. Pass RetryPolicy.none() to disable. Off by default.

    • autoRetryPolicy

      public RetryPolicy autoRetryPolicy()

    • setConcurrency

      public void setConcurrency(int parallelTransfers)
      Sets how many files transfer in parallel (>= 1; clamped up to 1). The default of 1 preserves the original sequential behaviour. Takes effect the next time the worker starts (startWorker()); a running queue must be stopped and restarted to change it. Note the bandwidth throttle (setMaxBytesPerSecond(long)) measures rate per active file, so with concurrency > 1 the effective cap is approximate.
